name: Helping models know what they actually know
gist: These papers work on making models give honest confidence about their answers and admit uncertainty instead of guessing confidently when they do not actually know.
explain: When a model is wrong, it usually sounds completely confident. You ask it a question, it generates an answer with full certainty, and later you discover the answer was hallucinated—the model made something up. Papers in this area work on calibration and uncertainty: teaching models to express genuine confidence when they know something and genuine doubt when they do not. The core idea is that if a model can admit uncertainty, downstream systems can decide whether to use the answer, ask a human, or search for more information instead of blindly trusting wrong answers.

The challenge is that calibration is separate from accuracy—a model can be accurate but overconfident, or accurate but underconfident. Papers study multiple approaches: some train models with confidence scores so they learn to output a number between 0 and 1 reflecting genuine uncertainty, others use ensemble methods where multiple models vote and disagreement indicates uncertainty, and others study how to extract uncertainty from the model's internal states during generation. The tricky part is that some uncertainties are learned during training and hard to change later.

The payoff is systems that are more reliable and trustworthy because they tell you when to trust them. In high-stakes applications like medicine or finance, knowing when a model is uncertain is as important as knowing when it is right because a wrong answer from a confident model is dangerous. Uncertainty estimates also help with efficiency: if you know a model is uncertain, you can route the query to a human expert or use a different method, saving resources because you do not waste time on low-confidence answers. This area also helps researchers understand what models have actually learned versus what they are just pattern-matching by looking at which answers the model is sure about, which reveals what is real understanding versus lucky guessing because true knowledge should be consistent.

papers.title: Calibrating Verbalized Confidence with Self-Generated Distractors
papers.contribution: Provides less saturated, more usable confidence estimates that better calibrate LLM outputs by leveraging coherence across validations on incompatible claims.

papers.title: CiteGuard: Conformal False-Discovery Control for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.contribution: Reduces false-discovery rate among accepted claims from 28-31% to below 10% at α=0.10, retaining 86-92% of supported claims with finite-sample guarantees.

papers.title: Correctness-Optimized Residual Activation Lens (CORAL): Transferrable and Calibration-Aware Inference-Time Steering
papers.contribution: Consistently improves accuracy by 10% and expected calibration error by 50% on average; transfers gains to held-out benchmarks without retraining with 14% accuracy and 49% ECE improvements.

papers.title: Don't Throw Away Your Beams: Improving Consistency-based Uncertainties in LLMs via Beam Search
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification performance with improved consistency and reduced variance compared to multinomial sampling.

papers.title: Expert Merging: Model Merging with Unsupervised Expert Alignment and Importance-Guided Layer Chunking
papers.contribution: Surpasses baselines across MLLM and LLM backbones with Expert Merging++ delivering further gains, sometimes exceeding supervised approaches.

papers.title: Extending the Context of Pretrained LLMs by Dropping Their Positional Embedding
papers.contribution: Enables seamless zero-shot context extension without long-context finetuning, outperforming rotary position embedding scaling methods across different model sizes.

papers.title: Trained on Tokens, Calibrated on Concepts: The Emergence of Semantic Calibration in LLMs
papers.contribution: Shows base LLMs are remarkably well-calibrated for semantic content in open-ended QA, while instruction-tuning and chain-of-thought reasoning systematically break this calibration.

papers.title: Why Keep Your Doubts to Yourself? Trading Visual Uncertainties in Multi-Agent Bandit Systems
papers.contribution: Agora achieves +8.5% accuracy over baselines on MMMU while reducing cost by over 3x across five multimodal benchmarks (MMMU, MMBench, MathVision, InfoVQA, CC-OCR).

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Are Time Series Foundation Models Well-Calibrated?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that time series foundation models are consistently better calibrated than baseline models and tend not to be systematically over- or under-confident.

papers.title: Beyond Heuristic Tuning: Power-Calibrated LLM Watermarking
papers.contribution: Derives practical parameter selection procedures achieving optimal trade-offs under constraints, validated across multiple language models with Pareto-optimal point identification.

papers.title: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Knowledge Grounding
papers.contribution: Achieves higher performance with reduced token usage compared to long-context approaches across diverse LLM architectures and six knowledge-intensive benchmarks.

papers.title: Beyond Raw Detection Scores: Markov-Informed Calibration for Boosting Machine-Generated Text Detection
papers.contribution: The method demonstrates significant gains over baselines with negligible computational overhead across cross-LLM and paraphrasing attack scenarios.

papers.title: Beyond Reactivity: Proactive Adaptive Conformal Inference for Online LLM Factuality
papers.contribution: Reduces deviation from target error rate by up to 60% and accelerates coverage recovery by 2.5x during abrupt shifts.

papers.title: Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers: Formalization and Measurement
papers.contribution: Fatigue Index is a lightweight model-agnostic diagnostic predicting task degradation (AUROC=0.95) and repetition (rho=0.94), revealing non-monotonic scaling where small instruction-tuned models collapse faster than base models.

papers.title: Domain-Shift-Aware Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Delivers more reliable coverage under substantial distribution shifts while maintaining efficiency; validated on MMLU benchmark.

papers.title: Efficient Hallucination Detection for LLMs Using Uncertainty-Aware Attention Heads
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification baselines across twelve datasets and nine LLMs with less than 1% additional computation, requiring neither labeled data nor parameter tuning.

papers.title: Eliciting Numerical Predictive Distributions of LLMs Without Auto-Regression
papers.contribution: Shows LLM embeddings carry informative signals about predictive distribution summary statistics including numerical uncertainty without sampling.

papers.title: Estimating Semantic Alphabet Size for LLM Uncertainty Quantification
papers.contribution: Provides more accurate semantic entropy estimation from few samples with high interpretability, flagging incorrect LLM responses effectively.

papers.title: From Guessing to Placeholding: A Cost-Theoretic Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Code Completion
papers.contribution: Reduces expected editing costs from 19% to 50% while preserving standard hard completion performance across 1.5B-14B models.

papers.title: Generalized Correctness Models: Learning Calibrated and Cross-Model Correctness Predictors from Historical Patterns
papers.contribution: Shows that reliable LLM confidence estimation is a cross-model skill learned by encoding prediction history, with effective generalization across model families and datasets.

papers.title: How to Correctly Report LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations
papers.contribution: Moreover, we show that our framework remains unbiased under distribution shift between the test and calibration datasets, in contrast to existing approaches

papers.title: Innovation: An Almost Characterization of Hallucination
papers.contribution: Innovation provides a theoretical characterization of hallucination tied to the missing mass measure of training data incompleteness.

papers.title: Logit-Attention Divergence: Mitigating Position Bias in Multi-Image Retrieval via Attention-Guided Calibration
papers.contribution: Training-free method improves permutation invariance and achieves over 40% accuracy enhancement compared to baselines on MS-COCO-based benchmarks.

papers.title: PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs
papers.contribution: Demonstrates the capability through case studies on theorem proving agents.

papers.title: Probability-Entropy Calibration: An Elastic Indicator for Adaptive Fine-tuning
papers.contribution: Consistent improvements on mathematical reasoning, transfer gains on OOD reasoning, and better code generation over probability- or entropy-only baselines.

papers.title: SCOPE: Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise LLM Judging
papers.contribution: Satisfies target risk bounds with empirical FDR ≈0.097-0.099 at alpha=0.10 and accepts up to 2.4x more judgments under the same risk constraint.

papers.title: SelfReflect: Can LLMs Communicate Their Internal Answer Distribution?
papers.contribution: Shows LLMs are incapable of revealing uncertainties through reasoning or finetuning alone, but can generate faithful summaries when sampling outputs and feeding back into context.

papers.title: The ACUTE Protocol: Operationalizing Language Model Activations for Better Calibration, Utility, and Trust
papers.contribution: Taken together, our work shows that equipping LLMs with the ACUTE protocol can improve calibration, utility, and trustworthiness in numerous settings..

papers.title: Training Prompt Matters: State-Adaptive Optimization for Robust Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting while improving generalization, achieving substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: When Model Merging Breaks Routing: Training-Free Calibration for MoE
papers.contribution: Effectively mitigates routing breakdown across diverse MoE merging baselines with substantial performance improvements on mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.

papers.title: Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment
papers.contribution: Outperforms averaging-based aggregation methods on NLG evaluation datasets with learned discriminators correlating strongly to cycle consistency of LLM judgments.
